overall.summary: Every number reproduces and the saddle, sodium U, brake, arm, detector and gate behave as stated; nothing is refuted. 7 statements are weakened: a fast heart rate raises risk only at low (not normal) pressure, age is not monotone when sodium is raised, diabetes acts through the brake about as much as through the gate, the brake is not the only cause of the fall at high pressure, the high-sodium arm opens inside the normal range, the low-sodium hinge opens at normal sodium under high pressure, and the smoker unit's hypothesis restates its formula.

direct_terms.why: The straight-line reading is right for age, creatinine and smoking, whose effects run mainly here; for sbp and heart rate the direct terms are not the model's effect (the brake and gate bend them into a saddle), and the concept is just the formula's three largest terms.

rate_pressure_brake.why: Confirmed as a brake that opens with a fast heart rate or high pressure and makes a fast rate low-risk at high pressure, though the high-pressure arm closing carries the first part of that fall.

high_sbp_low_hr_arm.why: Confirmed as hypertension with a relatively slow heart rate raising risk, opening at a higher pressure the faster the heart rate (sbp 128 at 55 bpm, 151 at 75, off at 95).

high_hr_low_sbp_detector.why: Confirmed as a tachycardia detector switched off by high pressure (opens about 74 bpm at sbp 120, about 100 bpm at sbp 160), the shock-index pattern.

high_sodium_arm.why: A real high-sodium arm, but it opens at about 140 mmol/L inside the normal range, so the 'hypernatraemia' reading covers only the top of where it acts.

male_unit.why: Confirmed: male sex raises the predicted risk only when the shock gate is open (22% to 42% at heart rate 100, sbp 120; no change in the typical case).

smoker_unit.why: A copy of the smoking input with a negligible push on the gate (AUC unchanged); the reading is the sign of its weight, and smoking's effect lives in the direct term.
